mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market confidence and equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the monthly employment increase (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,600 in a month, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, as rising consumer demand anticipates stronger corporate earnings.
failure_condition: Over 50 test windows with HOUST > 1600, 20-day forward returns are not statistically above the mean of non-trigger windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary pressures.
failure_condition: During INDPRO declines of ≥2%, 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than during stable INDPRO periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased labor market strength and equity risk premium compression.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns during the trigger are not higher than the 5-day average of the previous 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% and 5% respectively over the next quarter are required to generate a positive S&P 60-day forward return via dual demand channel amplification.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > (current + 2%) AND RSAFS > (current + 5%) over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 60-day returns when only one of the proxies increases (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling UNRATE below 3%, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to increased recession risk and reduced equity valuation sensitivity to earnings growth.
failure_condition: During the low-unemployment regime, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during high-unemployment regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as markets anticipate lower discount rates and improved equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: During CPIAUCSL < 2 months, 20-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day moving average of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).
